summary: South Africa's Department of Home Affairs publishes a visa exemption list setting out, for each nationality and passport category, whether a port of entry visa is needed and for how long the exemption applies (90 days for every category of US passport, for example). It launched an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) on 12 August 2026, piloted for travellers from China, India, Indonesia and Mexico and initially available for arrivals at the OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports. Home Affairs requires at least one blank passport page for endorsements.

overstay.text: Under the Immigration Act, a foreigner who leaves South Africa after the visa has expired is dealt with under section 30(1)(h), which covers a person who has overstayed the prescribed number of times. Under the Immigration Regulations, an overstayer may be declared undesirable for 12 months if the overstay does not exceed 30 days, for two years for a second overstay within 24 months, and for five years if the overstay exceeds 30 days. The overstay is counted from the date of expiry of the last valid visa. Anyone who enters, remains in or departs from the Republic in contravention of the Act commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine or to imprisonment of up to two years. The Act does not state the fine amount. A person declared undesirable under these sections must submit a written representation to the Department of Home Affairs.

idp.text: South Africa is a party to the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). South Africa's embassy in Paris says that to drive in South Africa, foreigners must have a full licence from their country of residence, that licences printed in English are valid, and that an International Driver's Permit (IDP) must be obtained if the licence is in any other language. faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for South Africa?
faq.answer: No. Home Affairs' visa exemption list gives 90 days for every category of US passport. Its requirements for entering South Africa include a valid passport for the intended stay with at least one blank page for endorsements, sufficient funds for day-to-day expenses and a return or onward ticket.

faq.answer: At least one blank page for entry and departure endorsements, according to the Department of Home Affairs; UK travel advice says two.

faq.answer: Home Affairs says that visa applicants with children travelling with them or joining them must provide unabridged birth certificates, proof of guardianship or custody, or the guardian's consent for an unaccompanied minor. The UK FCDO says there are special requirements for travelling to South Africa with children aged 17 and under and for unaccompanied children, and Canada says unaccompanied minors under 18 are subject to additional requirements.

levies.air-passenger-tax.text: The Air Passenger Tax (APT) is a fee that people travelling by plane pay when flying out of South Africa. The tax helps support air travel infrastructure and is a common international practice. In South Africa, airlines are responsible for collecting the Air Passenger Tax from travellers and then paying it over to SARS.
Currently, as of 2025, the tax is:
R100 for flights to countries in the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) — like Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, and Eswatini.
R190 for flights to other international destinations.
The tax is not applicable to domestic flights. It is only applicable to chargeable passengers leaving on an international flight.
More information about this is available on Section 47(B) of the Customs and Excise Act No. 91 of 1964.
Standard rate departures are R190 per ticket (for a destination other than SACU countries)
Lower rate departures to BLNS countries (Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland) are R100 per ticket.
